intro: Nevada runs elections county by county, through each county clerk or registrar of voters, with the Secretary of State overseeing the state.

id_rule.text: Same-day registration requires an unexpired Nevada driver's license, Nevada ID card, Nevada DMV interim document, or Tribal ID, plus proof of address if your ID does not show your current address. A first-time registrant whose ID number did not match DMV or Social Security records must show ID before voting. That can be a photo ID with your name and current address, or a bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government document that shows your name and current address.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register by mail or in person with your county
dates.detail: Applications sent by mail, through a government agency, or in person to your county election office were due by this date. After this, you can still register the same day you vote.

src.label: Clark County (NV) Registrar of Voters, notice of close of registration, 2026 general

dates.label: Mail ballots sent to voters
dates.detail: Nevada mails a ballot to each active registered voter who did not opt out. Counties must start mailing to in-state voters no later than 20 days before Election Day.

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Vote in person at an early voting site. Counties pick their own sites and hours. You can register and vote the same day during early voting.

dates.label: Last day to register or update online and still get a mail ballot
dates.detail: Register or update at RegisterToVote.NV.gov by 11:59 pm, with a Nevada driver's license or DMV ID. If you register online from Oct. 21 on, you vote a provisional ballot in person.

src.label: Clark County (NV) Registrar of Voters, notice of close of registration, 2026 general

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 7 pm. You can register and vote the same day at a vote center. A mail ballot must be postmarked by Election Day, or put in a drop box by the close of polls.

dates.label: Mail ballots must arrive
dates.detail: A mailed ballot must be postmarked by Nov. 3 and received by your county election office by 5 pm on Nov. 7 (the fourth day after Election Day).
